subject: english-language
title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Language A (4EA1)

papers.name: Paper 1: Non-fiction Texts and Transactional Writing
papers.materials: Insert (Text One). Text Two is from Part 1 of the Anthology: use your own copy, as it is not reprinted in this practice paper.
instructions: Use black ink or ball-point pen.
Answer ALL questions in Section A and ONE question from Section B.
Write your answers in the spaces provided; there may be more space than you need.
information: The total mark for this paper is 90.
The marks for each question are shown in brackets: use them to judge how long to spend on each question.
In Section B you will be assessed on your vocabulary, spelling, punctuation and grammar as well as on your writing for the task.
advice: Read each question carefully before you begin your answer.
Spend about 1 hour 30 minutes on Section A and about 45 minutes on Section B.
Leave time at the end to check your answers.

sections.title: SECTION A: Reading
sections.instructions: Answer ALL questions in this section. You should spend about 1 hour and 30 minutes on this section. The questions are based on Text One (in the Insert) and Text Two (from Part 1 of the Anthology).

sections.title: SECTION B: Transactional Writing
sections.instructions: Answer ONE question in this section. You should spend about 45 minutes on your chosen question.

qtypes.label: Select two words or phrases (Q1)
qtypes.description: Pick two words or phrases from a few given lines of the unseen text.

qtypes.label: In your own words (Q2)
qtypes.description: Describe or explain what happens in a given section of the unseen text, in your own words.

qtypes.label: Explain with brief quotations (Q3)
qtypes.description: Explain thoughts, feelings or what we learn from a given section of the unseen text.

qtypes.label: Language and structure, anthology text (Q4)
qtypes.description: Analyse how the writer of the anthology text uses language and structure for a stated effect.

qtypes.label: Compare the two texts (Q5)
qtypes.description: Compare how the writers of the unseen and anthology texts present their ideas and perspectives.

qtypes.label: Complete Section A (Q1-Q5)
qtypes.description: One unseen text and one anthology text with all five reading questions, as in the real paper.

qtypes.label: Transactional writing task
qtypes.description: One writing task with a given form, audience and purpose (AO4 27 + AO5 18).

qtypes.label: Section B: choice of two tasks
qtypes.description: Two transactional tasks in different forms; the candidate answers one.

topics.title: Reading the unseen text: retrieval and interpretation (AO1)

subtopics.title: Selecting words and phrases
subtopics.summary: Find two short quotations that answer the question, taken only from the lines given.

points.summary: Stay inside the line numbers given in the question.
Copy words or phrases exactly; no explanation is needed.

subtopics.title: Describing and explaining in your own words
subtopics.summary: Make four separate, accurate points about a section of the text, rephrased in your own words.

points.summary: Pick out the key events, facts or ideas in a given section.
Rephrase them rather than copying long chunks of the text.

subtopics.title: Explaining thoughts, feelings and ideas
subtopics.summary: Explain five points about what a writer thinks, feels or shows, backed by short quotations.

points.summary: Interpret what the writer thinks and feels, not just what happens.
Support points with short, well-chosen quotations.

topics.title: Language and structure in the anthology texts (AO2)

subtopics.title: Analysing language and structure in a Part 1 anthology text
subtopics.summary: Explain how a writer's word choices, imagery, sentences and organisation create a stated effect on the reader.

points.summary: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, The Danger of a Single Story: how a single, narrow story about a people or place creates stereotypes.
George Alagiah, A Passage to Africa: suffering, dignity and the relationship between a reporter and the people he reports on.
Kari Herbert, The Explorer's Daughter: the Arctic landscape, the hunt for narwhal and the writer's mixed feelings about it.
Steven Morris, Explorers or boys messing about? Either way, taxpayer gets rescue bill: risk-taking adventurers, their rescue and the cost to the public.
Aron Ralston, 127 Hours: Between a Rock and a Hard Place: danger, survival and determination in a remote canyon.
Benjamin Zephaniah, Young and dyslexic? You've got it going on: dyslexia, education and self-belief.
Emma Levine, A Game of Polo with a Headless Goat: the excitement and chaos of an unusual sporting event.
Jamie Zeppa, Beyond the Sky and the Earth: A Journey into Bhutan: arriving in a new country and her impressions of its landscape, people and history.
Helen Macdonald, H is for Hawk: a first, intense encounter with a wild bird.
Adeline Yen Mah, Chinese Cinderella: a child's longing for her father's approval.

topics.title: Comparing the unseen and anthology texts (AO3)

subtopics.title: Comparing writers' ideas and perspectives
subtopics.summary: Compare what two writers think and feel about a shared subject and how they get it across.

points.summary: Find similarities and differences in the writers' ideas, attitudes and experiences.
Compare how they present them: tone, language and structure.
Keep references balanced across both texts.

subtopics.title: All five reading questions on one pair of texts
subtopics.summary: Practise the whole of Section A: three questions on the unseen text, one on the anthology text and the comparison.

points.summary: Manage 90 minutes across 45 marks, giving most time to the 12- and 22-mark questions.
